title: Describe people and compare real options
lessons:
## Your communication goal
Describe a person without stereotyping, compare two practical options, and justify a choice with a limitation. You will listen to a housing discussion, read offers, ask follow-up questions, and recommend an option. These are learning tasks, not calibrated TCF questions.

## Before you begin
You need subject pronouns, present-tense forms of être and avoir, articles, questions, negation, and basic prices. Quick check: say who you are, describe your home, and ask its rent without notes. If these are difficult, review them briefly: `Je suis locataire.` — I am a tenant. `Il y a deux chambres.` — There are two bedrooms. `Quel est le loyer ?` — What is the rent? A description normally uses être plus an adjective, not avoir: `La pièce est lumineuse.` — The room is bright.

## 1. Build an accurate description
An adjective describes a noun and normally agrees with that noun in gender and number. Often add -e for feminine and -s for plural: `un voisin patient`, `une voisine patiente`, `des voisines patientes` — a patient male neighbour, a patient female neighbour, patient female neighbours. Many final consonants are silent; an added feminine ending can make one audible. An adjective already ending in -e usually keeps that spelling in the feminine: `un collègue calme`, `une collègue calme` — a calm colleague. An adjective ending in -s or -x usually adds nothing in masculine plural: `des bureaux spacieux` — spacious offices.

Learn frequent patterns as pairs: `sportif, sportive` — sporty; `heureux, heureuse` — happy; `ancien, ancienne` — former/old; `cher, chère` — expensive/dear; `blanc, blanche` — white; `public, publique` — public; `doux, douce` — soft/gentle; `long, longue` — long. With beau, nouveau and vieux, learn the special masculine singular form before a vowel or silent h: `un bel appartement`, `un nouvel emploi`, `un vieil hôtel` — a beautiful apartment, a new job, an old hotel. Feminine forms are belle, nouvelle, vieille; masculine plurals are beaux, nouveaux, vieux. Do not invent an -s plural for beau.

Most descriptive adjectives follow the noun: `une cuisine moderne` — a modern kitchen. Common size, age and evaluation adjectives often precede it: `un petit jardin` — a small garden. Meaning can change: `mon ancien bureau` — my former office; `un meuble ancien` — an antique piece of furniture. Colour adjectives usually agree: `des portes vertes` — green doors. Noun-based orange and marron normally remain unchanged: `des chaises orange` — orange chairs. Compound colours also stay unchanged: `des rideaux bleu clair` — light-blue curtains. Adverbs do not agree: `Elles sont vraiment disponibles.` — They are really available.

## 2. Compare the right thing
For adjectives and adverbs, use plus/aussi/moins + adjective or adverb + que: `Ce trajet est moins fatigant que l'autre.` — This journey is less tiring than the other one. `Elle explique plus clairement que moi.` — She explains more clearly than I do. For quantities, use plus de/autant de/moins de + noun + que: `Ce quartier a autant de commerces que le centre.` — This neighbourhood has as many shops as the centre. For actions, put the comparison after the verb: `Je marche davantage ici.` — I walk more here. You can also say `Je travaille autant que toi.` — I work as much as you do. Do not use aussi de for equal quantities.

Bon describes a noun; bien usually describes an action. Their common comparatives differ: `Ce siège est meilleur.` — This seat is better. `J'entends mieux ici.` — I hear better here. Not plus bon or plus bien. `Cette solution est pire.` — This solution is worse. Plus mauvais is also possible; do not treat every alternative as an error. Superlatives identify the top or bottom of a group: `C'est la salle la plus calme du bâtiment.` — It is the quietest room in the building. `C'est le meilleur compromis.` — It is the best compromise. Keep the article aligned with the noun: la salle, les salles les plus calmes.

## 3. Choose without overclaiming
Use a criterion, evidence, and a trade-off: `Je préfère le studio parce qu'il est proche du métro, mais il manque de rangement.` — I prefer the studio because it is near the metro, but it lacks storage. `Cela dépend de votre budget.` — That depends on your budget. Compare what an offer actually states; cheap does not automatically mean poor quality. English traps: `une personne sympathique` means a nice person, not necessarily a sympathetic listener; `une bibliothèque` is a library, not a bookshop. Use `Elle a les cheveux courts.` — She has short hair, with a definite article for a physical description, not an English-style possessive by default.

## 4. Listen and speak clearly
Hear the contrast in `grand / grande`, `petit / petite`, `heureux / heureuse`. The final consonant is not always pronounced in the masculine but becomes audible in these feminine forms. In `plus cher`, plus usually has a silent s; in `plus agréable`, hear a z liaison. Standalone plus meaning more can have a pronounced s. Learn the whole phrase rather than one universal pronunciation. Use the French voice to compare, then speak without the text. Browser voices are synthetic and do not reproduce all natural accents or exam conditions. If playback fails, text study is useful but is not completed listening.

## 5. Attempt before revealing
A. Describe two bright rooms with the feminine plural of lumineux. B. Compare the number of windows using fewer. C. Translate: This chair is better, but I work better standing. D. Choose between a spacious flat far from work and a small flat nearby; give a reason and a disadvantage.

:::answer
A. `Deux pièces lumineuses.` — Two bright rooms. B. `Ce logement a moins de fenêtres que l'autre.` — This home has fewer windows than the other one. C. `Cette chaise est meilleure, mais je travaille mieux debout.` — This chair is better, but I work better standing. D. One possible answer: `Je choisis le petit appartement, car le trajet est court. En revanche, je manque de place pour recevoir mes amis.` — I choose the small apartment because the journey is short. However, I lack space to host my friends. Other well-supported choices are valid.
:::

## 6. Four-skill work and cumulative review
Do both listening tasks with the script hidden; note the criterion that changes the decision, not every word. Read both offers before choosing. For speaking, use a new situation and no memorized paragraph. For writing, revise adjective endings only after checking audience and purpose. Recycle earlier questions, quantities and directions: ask the price, locate the entrance, and explain a need. Bank items 001–025 focus on description, 026–050 on comparison, 051–075 on practical choices, and 076–100 on transfer. Their purposes tell you what to do; a model is not the only correct oral response.

## 7. Retrieval and spacing
Spread the bank over four sessions of 25 items. Within a four-hour study day, try 35 minutes of recall/form work, 45 listening, 40 reading, 45 speaking, 45 writing and 30 error review; adjust rather than treating this split as a rule. Revisit missed items after one day, three days, seven days and two weeks. Log the phrase, your error, a corrected example and the next review date. If agreement fails, sort nouns by gender and say adjective pairs; if comparison fails, identify whether you compare a quality, quantity or action. On review day, describe an unfamiliar room and justify a fresh choice. Completion and self-ratings do not establish an official language level.

activities.title: A flat with a trade-off
activities.prompt: Listen without reading. Why does the speaker prefer the second flat?
activities.script: J'ai visité deux appartements. Le premier est plus grand et sa cuisine est neuve. Pourtant, je préfère le deuxième. Il est un peu plus cher, mais je peux aller au travail à pied. La chambre donne sur une cour calme. Le seul vrai problème, c'est le rangement : il n'y a qu'un petit placard.
activities.explanation: The speaker can walk to work from the second flat. The first has the new kitchen; the second is more expensive and lacks storage.

activities.title: Recommend a workshop
activities.prompt: Listen for the criterion that matters most to the customer.
activities.script: Bonjour, je cherche un atelier de cuisine pour mon père. Il cuisine déjà très bien, mais il entend mal dans les grands groupes. Notre atelier du mardi accueille huit personnes, contre seize le samedi. Il est moins varié et un peu plus cher. Alors, je choisis le mardi. L'important, c'est qu'il puisse suivre les explications.
options: A small group where explanations are easier to hear.
activities.explanation: The father's hearing makes group size decisive. Tuesday costs more and offers less variety; he is already a good cook.

activities.title: Two bike offers
activities.prompt: Read both offers. Which conclusion is supported?
activities.passage: Vélo A : cadre léger, neuf kilos, trois vitesses. Garantie de deux ans. Aucun porte-bagages. Prix : 420 dollars. Vélo B : cadre renforcé, quatorze kilos, sept vitesses. Porte-bagages inclus. Garantie d'un an. Prix : 390 dollars. Livraison non comprise pour les deux modèles.
options: Bike A is cheaper and has more gears.
Bike B is lighter and has a longer warranty.
Bike B is cheaper and includes a luggage rack.
activities.explanation: B costs 390 rather than 420 dollars and includes a rack. A is lighter and has the longer warranty. Neither includes delivery.

activities.title: A colleague's recommendation
activities.prompt: What is the writer's main reservation?
activities.passage: Je te recommande la salle des Peupliers pour la réunion. Elle est moins centrale que celle du musée, mais beaucoup plus calme. Les tables sont réglables et l'entrée est accessible. En revanche, le dernier autobus part à dix-neuf heures. Pour une rencontre en soirée, il faut prévoir une autre solution de transport.
activities.explanation: The late transport limitation is explicit. Quiet, adjustable tables and an accessible entrance are presented as advantages.

activities.title: Choose a shared workspace
activities.prompt: You and a friend need a workspace. Invent two different options, compare cost, noise and access, ask two questions about your friend's priorities, then recommend one with a disadvantage. Speak from keywords, not a script. These are learning timings, not an official test task.
activities.model: Tu préfères travailler près de chez toi ou près du métro ? Quel budget peux-tu consacrer au bureau ? Le premier espace est moins cher, mais assez bruyant. Le deuxième est plus calme et ses horaires sont souples. Je préfère le deuxième parce que nous avons souvent des appels. En revanche, il faut réserver une place à l'avance. Si le prix est trop élevé pour toi, nous pouvons choisir seulement deux jours par semaine.
rubric: Fulfillment: compares two options and asks two relevant questions.
Coherence: states criteria, recommendation and drawback.
Range: uses quality and quantity comparisons appropriately.
Control: checks adjective agreement and meilleur versus mieux.
Intelligibility: phrases are audible; pauses do not obscure the recommendation.

activities.title: Recommend accommodation
activities.prompt: Write an email to a visiting friend comparing two invented places to stay. Describe useful features, state a recommendation, explain a limitation and ask which criterion matters most. Use 80–120 words; this is a learning task, not a full-format exam item.
activities.model:
Salut Inès,
J'ai deux idées pour ton séjour. Le studio près du parc est lumineux et moins cher que l'hôtel du centre. Il possède une petite cuisine, mais il est assez loin de la gare. L'hôtel est plus pratique pour les transports et son accueil est ouvert toute la nuit. En revanche, les chambres sont petites et le petit-déjeuner coûte cher. Je te conseille le studio parce que tu aimes cuisiner et marcher. Quel critère compte le plus pour toi : le prix ou la proximité des transports ? Dis-moi ce que tu préfères.
À bientôt,
Sam
rubric: Fulfillment: describes two places, recommends, qualifies and asks a question.
Organization: comparison is easy to follow.
Range: includes descriptive vocabulary and varied comparisons.
Control: agreement, articles and comparison structures are accurate enough for clarity.
Register: friendly email with a suitable opening and closing.
